articles.title: Intermittent or Continuous Renal-Replacement Therapy in Acute Kidney Injury.
articles.source: The New England journal of medicine
articles.summary: In this multicenter, open-label, noninferiority trial, we randomly assigned critically ill adults with acute kidney injury who had indications for renal-replacement therapy to undergo intermittent hemodialysis or continuous renal-replacement therapy as the initial treatment. The primary outcome was a major adverse kidney event - defined as death, dependence on renal-replacement therapy, or a serum creatinine concentration more than 25% above the baseline value - by day 90. A total of 554 patients underwent randomization, with 272 patients assigned to undergo intermittent hemodialysis and 282 to undergo continuous renal-replacement therapy; 535 patients (260 in the intermittent group and 275 in the continuous group) were included in the intention-to-treat population. A major adverse kidney event occurred by day 90 in 203 patients (78.1%) in the intermittent group and in 197 patients (71.6%) in the continuous group (adjusted absolute risk difference, 6.28 percentage points; 95% confidence interval [CI], -1.22 to 13.79). Death by day 90 occurred in 164 patients (63.1%) and in 147 patients (53.5%), respectively.

articles.title: Long-Lasting Mental Disorders in Caregivers of ICU Sepsis Survivors and Their Association With Patients' Post-Intensive Care Syndrome: A Prospective Multicenter Cohort Study.
articles.summary: Caregivers were a median of 67 years old (55-79 yr old), 31 (33.0%) were male, and 41 (43.6%) were spouses. Patients were a median of 74 years old (69-82 yr old), and 54 (57.4%) were male. The prevalence of mental PICS-F did not decrease from 3 to 12 months (43% vs. 42%, respectively), whereas the presence of PICS symptoms in patients decreased from 82% to 62%. In mixed-effects logistic regression, the presence of PICS symptoms in patients was significantly associated with PICS-F (adjusted odds ratio, 3.00; 95% CI, 1.54-5.88; p < 0.01).
